content.title: A pure-Go HTML to PDF converter
content.lede: gowkhtmltopdf is a clean-room, pure-Go work-alike for wkhtmltopdf that turns server-generated HTML and templates into multi-page PDFs and images. It is built as an HTML template engine for styled documents: invoices, receipts, certificates, storybooks, posters, tables, and multi-page documents with headers, footers, TOCs, and PDF outlines.

items.title: v0.2.2
items.body: The current release (`VERSION`, stamped into the CLI). Phases 0-9 plus the print CSS subset (tiers 1-2): load, parse, style, layout, paginate, paint, and PNG/JPEG image mode. Default write is unclaimed PDF 1.4. Opt-in `--pdf-version` 1.7 / 2.0 and `--pdf-profile` (PDF/A-3a, PDF/A-4, PDF/UA-1, PDF/UA-2) ship in this release.

items.title: Repeatable layout
items.body: The same HTML, settings, and fonts produce the same layout. Default CLI PDF bytes are not hash-stable: `/CreationDate` and `[date]`/`[time]` use the wall clock unless the library caller injects `Now`. The 10-page invoice gate still asserts page count and a generous CI budget of under 5 s.

items.title: Two static binaries
items.body: `gowkhtmltopdf` (PDF) and `gowkhtmltoimage` (PNG/JPEG) build with `CGO_ENABLED=0` into statically linked ELF/Mach-O executables with no native runtime library requirements. The first build may download the allowlisted pure-Go module graph; later builds can run offline with the cache populated.

items.title: MIT licensed
items.body: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Chinmay Sawant. This is an independent reimplementation: the project does not link to or redistribute wkhtmltopdf, Qt, or WebKit (wkhtmltopdf itself is LGPL).

sections.heading: Clean-room rewrite
sections.body: This codebase is not a binding to wkhtmltopdf/Qt/WebKit and not a wrapper around any commercial HTML-to-PDF API. The full pipeline (load, parse, CSS, layout, paginate, paint, PDF write) is implemented in this repository.

sections.heading: Pure-Go runtime boundary
sections.body: Runtime code uses the Go standard library plus two allowlisted pure-Go direct modules: `github.com/go-text/typesetting` for OpenType shaping and `github.com/tdewolff/canvas` for SVG rasterization. There are no third-party PDF/HTML/CSS APIs, no Chrome/WebKit embedding, and no cgo. Retain upstream notices for these dependencies and bundled fonts when preparing a redistribution archive.

sections.heading: AI-assisted development
sections.body: gowkhtmltopdf was developed using modern AI-assisted software engineering practices, pairing human architectural guidance with advanced reasoning and coding models (including Grok, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor) across planning, implementation, and validation.
bullets: Architecture & Planning: Comprehensive phase ledgers under `plans/`, API contracts, threat modeling, and scope boundaries were defined upfront to guide clean-room execution.

Core Engine Implementation: Tolerant HTML parsing, print CSS cascade, layout tree pagination, font shaping, and Flate/zlib PDF object serialization were developed with extensive AI-assisted pair programming.
Quality & Verification: All subsystems are verified against rigorous golden fixture visual tests (`make samples`), upstream bug dossiers, and benchmark regression suites.

sections.heading: The OSS story
sections.body: gowkhtmltopdf is MIT licensed under Chinmay Sawant and requires Go 1.26+. It is an independent clean-room reimplementation of the wkhtmltopdf CLI and behavior, so it shares none of wkhtmltopdf's LGPL obligations and does not ship Qt or WebKit. The current generic CLI (2026-08-14) is faster than wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1 at every tested size (16x at 2 pages, 1.6x at 500 pages). Peak RSS is lower through 100 pages and higher from 200 pages.

content.title: Scope boundary: an HTML template engine, not a browser
content.body: gowkhtmltopdf converts server-generated HTML and styled templates into multi-page PDFs without a browser process. There is no JavaScript, CSS support is a documented subset (flex, grid, and positioning are partial), and pixel parity with Chrome or WebKit is not a goal. Use it for invoices, certificates, storybooks, posters, tables, and multi-page documents with headers, footers, TOCs, and PDF outlines.
